target_customer: Mobile game developers who integrate the recording SDK, later consumers and advertisers on its streaming app
problem: Mobile gamers could not easily record and share gameplay, and developers wanted viral sharing inside their games.
business_model: Free SDK for developers, later virtual goods in a live streaming community and ads
product_category: Mobile gameplay recording SDK and live streaming

founders.name: Aditya Rathnam
education: MIT alumni (TechCrunch Aug 2012 calls the founders MIT alumni, wording ambiguous)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Adi Rathnam as Founder/CEO.

founders.name: Kevin Wang
founders.background_notes: YC page: algorithmic trader at Jump Trading after college; after the Lyft acquihire he spent four years at Lyft and in 2023 co-founded Mantel.

exit.reason: Acquihire: Lyft hired most of the team and did not buy the company or technology; products were wound down. CEO cited market size limits.

technical_complexity.rationale: Capturing OpenGL frames and encoding video on phones at low overhead was nontrivial, and the first version supported only the cocos2d engine, with Unity planned.

defensibility.rationale: Integration into many games gave reach, but the SDK was replaceable and Apple later shipped native recording.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform owners were the identified threat; Apple announced ReplayKit for iOS 9 in 2015. Kamcord then moved to live streaming and an app, and ended in a 2017 Lyft acquihire.

market_need_then: Mobile games were growing and developers wanted viral sharing; the 2012 beta drew 800 developer sign-ups and 22 integrated iOS games within about two months of launch (TechCrunch Aug 2012).

branding.community_and_virality: Gameplay videos shared from inside games carried the brand; a live streaming community reached 2M MAU per the YC page. No merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search found only trademark records; the brand was an SDK watermark more than a consumer name and no press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.to: Live streaming from any app and an activity stream
pivots.why: Round announcement said the focus expanded from mobile games to any app.

pivots.to: Mobile social app for editing and sharing screenshots and screen recordings (Flare)
pivots.why: Per YC page, three products in five years; reasons not stated.

outcome_analysis: Kamcord raised about 34 million dollars over four rounds and its SDK reached 200M devices, but the CEO said it hit market size limits at 2M monthly users after pivoting from games to streaming and then a screenshot app. Platform owners such as Apple added native recording, and Lyft hired most of the team in 2017 without buying the product.
notes: No company website listed. Dated competitor sources near the 2012 batch were not found (Everyplay by Applifier appears in undated trade coverage), so the list is empty. Series C valuation reported above 100 million dollars by one outlet, not recorded as post money. Total raised varies (22 to 38 million) across aggregators. YC invested 200K in June 2012 per one outlet, not recorded as a round. Series A and B were also covered by several outlets.
